name: Mastodon
summary: Mastodon lets anyone register an OAuth app with one unauthenticated API call, per server. The catch is federation: every user's server is a different authorization server, so you register dynamically, per instance.

verdict.label: Easy
verdict.headline: Fully agent-completable: apps are registered by an anonymous API call. Plan for one client per instance.

agent: Register an app via POST app_registration_endpoint (/api/v1/apps)
human: Each user signs in to their own instance and approves

steps.title: Ask the user for their instance
steps.detail: For example, mastodon.social or hachyderm.io. Store the client per instance.

steps.title: Fetch authorization server metadata
steps.detail: Mastodon 4.3+ publishes RFC 8414 metadata with a non-standard 'app_registration_endpoint' rather than 'registration_endpoint'.

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: POST /api/v1/apps with client_name, redirect_uris and scopes. Returns client_id and client_secret, with no auth needed.

evidence.note: We didn't POST, to avoid creating stray apps

steps.title: User authorizes
steps.detail: Redirect to /oauth/authorize with PKCE S256, then exchange the code at /oauth/token.

evidence.note: mastodon.social metadata fetched: PKCE S256, 47 scopes

blockers.symptom: Works on mastodon.social, fails on another server
blockers.cause: Client IDs are per-instance, or the server runs an older version without metadata.
blockers.fix: Register on every instance; fall back to /api/v1/apps directly if metadata is 404.

gotchas.title: Not standard DCR
gotchas.detail: Generic RFC 7591 clients look for 'registration_endpoint' and won't find it. Handle 'app_registration_endpoint' explicitly.

uncertainties: Behavior varies across forks (Pleroma, Misskey) and older Mastodon versions.
